title: Compound Component Pattern with Context Sharing
problemStatement: Implement `createCompoundAccordion()` with `Accordion(items)` and `Item(id, title, content)` that coordinates which panel is open without manual prop drilling.
interviewTrap: Passing `isOpen` and `onToggle` through multiple levels of parent-child-grandchild props creates fragile code. Compound components manage shared state implicitly.

testCases.name: Opens default item on initialization
testCases.testFn: const acc = createCompoundAccordion('1'); acc.addItem('1', 'T1', 'C1'); acc.addItem('2', 'T2', 'C2'); return acc.render()[0].isOpen;

testCases.name: Switches active open panel on toggle
testCases.input: toggle('2') closes panel 1 and opens panel 2
testCases.testFn: const acc = createCompoundAccordion('1'); acc.addItem('1', 'T1', 'C1'); acc.addItem('2', 'T2', 'C2'); acc.toggle('2'); const r = acc.render(); return [r[0].isOpen, r[1].isOpen];

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Passing an expensive component as the `children` prop `<Parent><ExpensiveTree /></Parent>` prevents `ExpensiveTree` from re-rendering when `Parent`'s state changes! Because `ExpensiveTree` is evaluated in the grandparent's render scope, its element reference is identical across `Parent` re-renders.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Compound Components (Tabs, Accordions, Menus).
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Compound Components (Tabs, Accordions, Menus) maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How do Compound Components (Tabs, Select, Accordion) communicate state implicitly?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Compound components use a shared internal React Context. The parent container (`<Tabs>`) holds state (active tab index) and exposes it via Context. Child components (`<Tabs.List>`, `<Tabs.Tab>`, `<Tabs.Panel>`) consume this Context implicitly without requiring the developer to pass props manually down the tree, providing clean and declarative component APIs.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The gold standard design system component architecture question.

realWorldUseCases.description: Building compound Tabs, Menus, Dialogs, and Accordions in design systems.
realWorldUseCases.companies: Radix UI, Headless UI, Material UI

howToExplain.opening: Compound Components work together as a synchronized unit, sharing implicit state via an internal Context to provide expressive, flexible component APIs.
keyPoints: Parent container manages state and provides internal Context.
Children implicitly consume state without manual prop drilling.
Allows arbitrary JSX composition and flexible markup structure.
Standard design pattern for enterprise UI component libraries.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Compound components offer the ultimate balance between flexible styling and encapsulated behavioral state.
analogies: An HTML <select> and <option> tag: they work together naturally without needing you to write wiring code between them.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using React.Children.map and cloneElement for compound components.
commonMistakes.why: cloneElement only reaches direct children; wrapping a child in a div breaks the entire component.
commonMistakes.correct: Use React Context for robust compound component communication.

followUpDeepDive.question: How do Radix Primitives and Ariakit enforce accessibility in compound components?
followUpDeepDive.answer: They combine compound context with WAI-ARIA attributes (`aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `role='tab'`) and roving tabindex keyboard focus handlers.
